# Glossary and FAQ {#glossary-and-faq}

This page defines the terms you meet when you operate or integrate the HeIMDALL DAQ chain, then answers the questions operators ask most often.

Part 1 is an alphabetical glossary. Part 2 is a practical FAQ.

## How to read this page {#how-to-read-this-page}

Every statement describes the code in this repository. Where it helps, a "Source:" line names the file that implements the behaviour.

Two markers separate today's behaviour from features that the scaling and clustering program adds:

- **Today** describes the code as it ships before the program's opt-in keys are set. It is also the behaviour you get when you leave every new key absent.
- **From this release** describes a feature added by the scaling and clustering program. Unless the text says otherwise, the feature is **opt-in**: it does nothing until you set a new config key, pass a new flag, or run a new tool. Leaving the new keys absent keeps today's behaviour byte for byte.

Glossary entries for brand-new concepts carry the label *(opt-in, added in this release)*.

Notation used throughout:

| Symbol | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `N` | `[federation] instance_id` of an instance |
| `<P>` | resource prefix: empty for N = 0, `inst<N>_` for N > 0 |
| `<off>` | port offset, `N * port_stride` |
| `M` | `[hw] num_ch`, the number of receiver channels |
| `fs` | `[daq] sample_rate`, the ADC sample rate in samples per second |
| `B` | `[daq] daq_buffer_size`, samples per channel in one DAQ block |
| `Ncpi` | `[pre_processing] cpi_size` |
| `R` | `[pre_processing] decimation_ratio` |
| `Nc` | `[calibration] corr_size` |

Five identifiers are easy to confuse. They answer different questions:

| Identifier | Set by | Unique within | Answers |
|---|---|---|---|
| `instance_id` | `[federation] instance_id` | one host | which prefixes and port offset this chain uses |
| `unit_id` | `[hw] unit_id` (header byte 24) | operator's choice | which physical unit produced a frame |
| node key *(this release)* | membership entry `host:instance_id` | the cluster | which chain a coordinator or router means |
| `node_id` *(this release)* | `[federation] node_id` | advisory | how a chain labels itself in STATUS, events and slot 108 |
| `cluster_id` *(this release)* | `[federation] cluster_id` | the network | which cluster a coordinator or member belongs to |

Related documents: `architecture.md`, `protocols.md`, `configuration.md`, `scaling_and_clustering.md`, `networking_and_time_sync.md`, `operations_runbook.md`, `capacity_planning.md`, `theory_coherent_acquisition.md`, `consumer_guide.md`, `hardware_setup.md`.

# Part 1: Glossary {#part-1-glossary}

## A {#a}

**A/B segments.** Every shared-memory hop has exactly two POSIX shared-memory objects, `<P><name>_A` and `<P><name>_B`, visible under `/dev/shm`. The producer writes one segment while the consumer reads the other. This is the "double buffer" of each hop. Source: `transport.c` (`num_buffers = 2`), `sh_mem_util.c`, `shmemIface.py`.

**A_BUFF_READY, B_BUFF_READY, INIT_READY, TERMINATE.** The single-byte messages of the FIFO signalling protocol. Their values are 1, 2, 10 and 255 in both C and Python. The producer writes `INIT_READY` once after it attaches, then `1` or `2` to hand over a filled segment, and `255` on shutdown. The consumer writes `1` or `2` back on the backward FIFO to free a segment. Source: `sh_mem_util.h`, `shmemIface.py`.

**ADC overdrive flags.** A per-channel bitmask in the IQ header (`adc_overdrive_flags`). rtl_daq sets a channel's bit when a block contains the byte value 255 (positive full scale). The code does not check the negative full-scale value 0, so the flag can miss clipping. rebuffer ORs the flags over the CPI. The gain-tuning state machine and the compression advisory read it. Source: `rtl_daq.c`, `rebuffer.c`.

**advertise_host** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. `[federation] advertise_host` is the host name an instance puts in its node key when it registers with a coordinator. Empty means the short lower-case host name. Set it when several hosts share an image name such as `raspberrypi`.

**AGC.** Automatic gain control of the R820T tuner. The `AGC ` verb on port 5001 (note the trailing space) and the ZMQ `a` command turn it on. rtl_daq forces manual gain at start because calibration needs a fixed gain. Source: `rtl_daq.c` (device setup in `main`), `hw_controller.py`.

**Aggregate channel power.** The mean power per sample across all channels. delay_sync computes it over the first `Nc` samples of each DATA frame, after the output correction (DC removal and IQ correction when `en_iq_cal = 1`), as `10*log10` in milli-dB. The reference is the digital full scale of the float samples, not dBm, so the value is signed and normally negative. delay_sync stamps it in reserved slot 101 while front-end telemetry is enabled. Every outbound frame carries the latest DATA value, so CAL and DUMMY frames repeat it. The orientation controller maximises it during scan-and-peak. Source: `delay_sync.py`, `iq_header.h`.

**allow_cidrs** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. `[federation] allow_cidrs` restricts which source addresses may connect to the coordinator (`:6000`) and the router stats port (`:7001`). Empty means everyone. Connections from outside the list are closed silently.

**amplitude_cal_mode.** `[calibration] amplitude_cal_mode` selects how IQ calibration sets channel magnitudes: `default` keeps the eigenvector magnitudes, `channel_power` equalises mean channel power, `disabled` corrects phase only. Source: `delay_sync.py`.

**amplitude_tolerance, phase_tolerance.** `[calibration]` thresholds, in whole dB and whole degrees. Shipped defaults are 2 dB and 1 degree. A check fails when a channel's phase correction exceeds ±`phase_tolerance`, or when its amplitude correction factor exceeds +`amplitude_tolerance` dB. A failed check triggers another IQ correction (during calibration) or counts as a sync failure (during tracking).

The amplitude test is one-sided. It triggers only when a channel is too weak, so that its correction factor is above `10^(tol/20)`. A channel that is too strong (correction factor below `10^(-tol/20)`, 0.794 at 2 dB) passes. The phase test is symmetric because it uses the absolute angle. Source: `delay_sync.py` (`STATE_IQ_CAL` and `STATE_TRACK` checks).

**Antenna profile.** The optional `[antenna]` section (`antenna_profile.py`): element gain in dBi, beamwidth, polarization, cable and connector loss, and a boresight offset. It feeds the link budget and the orientation boresight correction. Disabled by default (`en_antenna_profile = 0`).

**auth_token** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. `[federation] auth_token` is a shared secret. When set, every request to the coordinator and the router stats port must start with `AUTH <token> `. Empty (the default) means no authentication, which is today's behaviour.

**auto_config.py.** A start-script helper that rewrites a few config keys whose value is the literal `auto`. Today none of those keys exists in any shipped config, so it changes nothing. Source: `auto_config.py`.

## B {#b}

**Backpressure.** The flow-control mode in which a producer waits until the consumer frees a segment. The rtl_daq to rebuffer pipe and the rebuffer to decimate hop use it, so a slow stage there stalls the stage before it. Compare **drop mode**. Source: `daq_start_sm.sh` (`rebuffer.out 0`).

**Backward FIFO.** The named pipe `_data_control/<P>bw_<name>` that carries "segment free" bytes from consumer to producer. In drop mode the producer opens it with `O_NONBLOCK`.

**Bias tee.** A circuit that puts DC power on the antenna coax to feed an external LNA. `[hw] en_bias_tee` sets the start-up state per channel. With `[amplification] en_bias_tee_runtime = 1`, the `BIAS` verb changes it at run time through the ZMQ `b` command. rtl_daq drives GPIO `m+1` of the control-channel dongle for channel `m`. GPIO 0 is reserved for the noise source. Source: `rtl_daq.c` (bias-tee setup and the `b` command handler).

**Boresight offset.** The angle between the antenna's mechanical pointing and its electrical beam centre. `[antenna] boresight_az_offset_deg` and `boresight_el_offset_deg` correct commanded bearings.

**BUILD.** Make variable that selects compiler flags: `release` (default, `-Ofast -ffast-math -flto` on x86_64 and aarch64), `debug` (`-Og -g`) or `asan` (`-O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined`). Source: `Firmware/_daq_core/Makefile`.

**Burst.** See **noise burst**.

## C {#c}

**CAL frame.** Frame type 3. rtl_daq labels a frame CAL whenever the noise source is commanded on. A CAL frame carries exactly `Nc` samples per channel at the full ADC rate, because the decimator does not filter CAL frames. Its size differs from DATA frames on the same stream whenever `corr_size != cpi_size`; equal sizes are allowed, because ini_checker's `corr_size <= cpi_size` check is disabled, so use `frame_type`, not the size, to tell them apart. Its `sampling_freq` also differs when `R > 1`; at the shipped `R = 1` both frame types carry `adc_sampling_freq`. rebuffer emits one CAL frame per DAQ block, so `daq_block_index` advances by 1 between CAL frames. Source: `rebuffer.c`, `fir_decimate.c`.

**cal_frame_interval, cal_frame_burst_size.** In tracking mode 2, hw_controller switches the noise source on after `cal_frame_interval` tracked frames and off after `cal_frame_burst_size` more CAL frames. Shipped values are 687 and 10, which is one burst about every 300 s. Source: `hw_controller.py`.

**cal_track_mode.** `[calibration] cal_track_mode` selects how delay_sync checks calibration once locked. `0` never checks. `2` (shipped default) checks only the CAL frames of the periodic noise bursts. In modes 0 and 2 the sync flags on DATA frames are set to 1 without a measurement.

`1` runs the calibration test on live antenna data, on every DATA frame. It compares each frame's inter-channel phase and amplitude pattern with the pattern on the first DATA frame after lock. It also requires a sharp correlation peak (20 dB at a 100-sample lag; see **dynamic range**). On live data that pattern is the incoming signal's spatial signature, which depends on its direction, not only on the channel gains. Mode 1 therefore works only while one strong, wideband, stationary signal is present. A moving source, a changing scene, a narrowband signal (CW, a 12.5 kHz FM carrier) or no signal at all count as sync failures. Enough failures send delay_sync back to `STATE_INIT` and start a new noise burst. Most deployments should keep mode 2. Source: `delay_sync.py` (`STATE_TRACK_LOCK`, `STATE_TRACK`).

**Calibration gain table.** During a noise burst hw_controller sets every channel to a fixed gain chosen from the nearest of 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, 600, 700 or 1700 MHz. It restores the user gains after the burst. The table is hardcoded and has no config key. Source: `hw_controller.py`.

**Candidate (coordinator candidate)** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A coordinator process listed in `[federation] coordinator_candidates`. Candidates elect one leader among themselves. With the key empty there is one static coordinator, as today.

**Channel.** One RTL-SDR receiver inside a coherent unit. `[hw] num_ch` sets the count (5 for KrakenSDR). By default channel `i` opens the dongle whose EEPROM serial is `1000+i`; `[hw] serial_base` or `[hw] device_serials` change the mapping. Source: `device_map.c`, `rtl_daq.c`.

**Cluster** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A set of instances, possibly on several hosts, managed by one coordinator or one elected leader. A cluster has a `cluster_id`. A cluster is not coherent across units; see **island**.

**cluster_id** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. `[federation] cluster_id`, default `default`, up to 31 characters. Coordinators and members reject peers whose cluster id differs (`cluster_mismatch`). This stops two labs on one LAN from merging.

**Cluster member** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. An instance that belongs to a cluster's membership. Members come from `[federation] cluster_members`, the coordinator's `--instances` list, legacy `peer_list`, or `REGISTER`. Compare **peer**.

**cluster_members** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. `[federation] cluster_members` is the full membership list, including the instance itself, in `host:instance_id[@node_id]` form. Duplicates and loopback hosts are errors.

**Coherence.** Channels are coherent when their samples are aligned in time and their relative phase and amplitude are known and stable. Coherence is what makes direction finding and passive radar possible. In this chain it exists only between the channels of one unit, inside one rtl_daq and one delay_sync. See `theory_coherent_acquisition.md`.

**Compression flags.** A per-channel bitmask (reserved slot 96). It marks channels whose estimated LNA output level is within `p1db_margin_db` of the LNA's output-referred P1dB. The estimate is `[amplification] expected_input_dbm` (default -60 dBm) plus the LNA gain minus the feed loss. It is a static estimate from config values, not a measurement of received power, and it never changes gains. Source: `gain_budget.py` (`p1db_headroom_db`).

**Consumer, producer.** The two ends of a shared-memory hop. The producer creates the segments and the FIFOs' write side. The consumer maps the segments and frees them.

**Control channel.** The dongle whose serial equals `[daq] ctr_channel_serial_no` (default 1000). Its GPIO 0 drives the noise source and its GPIOs `1..M` drive the bias tees. If no dongle has that serial, rtl_daq warns and uses device index 0. Source: `rtl_daq.c` (control-channel lookup in `main`).

**Control plane.** Everything that changes or queries the chain rather than carrying samples: the port 5001 TCP server, the port 1130 ZMQ link, the port 5002 status server, the port 5003 event publisher and the federation services.

**Coordinator.** Three different things share this word:

| Meaning | Status | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| The `federation_coordinator.py` process | Today | Text protocol on port 6000 (`STATUS`, `FREQ`, `GAIN`, `INSTANCE <id> <cmd>`, `REBALANCE`, `PING`). No start script launches it. |
| The "elected coordinator" in `federation_health.py` | Today | The lowest healthy `instance_id`. It only emits a `coordinator_elected` event. No code acts on it. |
| The elected leader among coordinator candidates | *(opt-in, added in this release)* | Lease-based election; only the leader accepts mutating verbs. See **election**. |

Source: `federation_coordinator.py`, `federation_health.py`.

**coordinator_host.** `[federation] coordinator_host`. Before this release no runtime code read it. From this release new code uses it as the default target of `heimdall-ctl fleet` and as the `REGISTER` target.

**corr_size.** `[calibration] corr_size`, the number of samples per channel that calibration uses (`Nc`, shipped 65536). CAL frames carry exactly `Nc` samples. delay_sync uses the first `Nc` samples of a DATA frame for checks.

**CPI (coherent processing interval).** The block of samples per channel that downstream DSP processes as one unit. `[pre_processing] cpi_size` sets it after decimation (shipped 1048576). rebuffer collects `Ncpi * R` raw samples per channel for each DATA frame. The frame period is `Ncpi * R / fs`, 0.437 s at the shipped values. Source: `rebuffer.c`.

**cpi_index.** A header counter set by the decimator. It increments for every frame the decimator receives, including DUMMY frames and frames it then drops. A gap in `cpi_index` at the consumer means a drop at or after the decimator. Drops before the decimator do not show in it.

## D {#d}

**daq_block_index.** The header counter of USB DAQ blocks, set by rtl_daq. On a consumer frame it is the index of the last block in the CPI, so it advances by `Ncpi * R / B` between consecutive DATA frames (4 at the shipped values), not by 1. It jumps further on the first DATA frame after a DUMMY run or a CAL burst, because rebuffer discards its partial CPI there. CAL frames advance it by 1. rtl_daq stamps an index on every block, including overrun blocks, so a USB overrun does not show as a skipped index.

**DAQ block.** The unit of USB acquisition: `B` samples per channel (`[daq] daq_buffer_size`, shipped 262144, must be a power of two). The block period is `B / fs`, 109 ms at the shipped values. rtl_daq emits one frame per block, once every channel has completed that block.

**daq_db, schema generation.** The optional BerkeleyDB telemetry store (`[database] en_db`). Its on-disk format is schema generation 2. A marker file `_schema_version` in `db_dir` records the generation. A read-write open of a database with any other marker deletes the old files, because the data is rolling telemetry. A read-only open raises instead. Source: `daq_db.py`, `daq_db_records.py`.

**DATA frame.** Frame type 0. A normal frame of `Ncpi` samples per channel, decimated by `R`, at `sampling_freq = fs / R`.

**Data plane.** The sample path: rtl_daq to rebuffer (stdout pipe), rebuffer to decimate, decimate to delay_sync, delay_sync to the consumer (shared memory or iq_server).

**Decimation ratio.** `[pre_processing] decimation_ratio` (`R`). decimate.out low-pass filters DATA frames with the FIR from `fir_coeffs.txt` and keeps every `R`th sample. With `R = 1` (shipped) the FIR is bypassed and the decimator only converts u8 samples to complex float32. `fir_tap_size` must exceed `R` when `R > 1`.

**delay_sync.** The Python stage `delay_sync.py`. It estimates and corrects inter-channel delays and IQ (amplitude and phase) differences, runs the sync state machine, writes the consumer output, and hosts the status server, event publisher and federation health thread.

**delay_sync_flag, iq_sync_flag.** Two header flags set by delay_sync. `delay_sync_flag = 1` means the frame is considered sample-aligned. `iq_sync_flag = 1` means its amplitude and phase are considered corrected. Both are 0 on DUMMY frames. In tracking modes 0 and 2 they are 1 on DATA frames without a fresh measurement. Source: `delay_sync.py`.

**device_serials, serial_base** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. `[hw] serial_base` makes channel `i` open serial `serial_base + i`. `[hw] device_serials` lists one serial per channel and wins over `serial_base`. Absent keys keep the default `1000+i` rule. When you set either key, also set `[daq] ctr_channel_serial_no` to one of the resolved serials, normally the unit's first serial (for example 1100 for unit 1). That dongle switches the unit's noise source and bias tees. ini_checker rejects a config where it is not one of the channel serials, and `provision_instance.py` writes it as the new serial at the template's control-channel index (the first serial with the shipped template). See also **set_unit_serials.sh**.

**Double-buffered shared memory.** The data-plane hop design: two segments (A and B) per hop, a forward FIFO to announce a filled segment and a backward FIFO to free it. The producer never writes a segment the consumer still holds. See **A/B segments**.

**Drop mode.** A flow-control mode in which the producer skips a frame when both segments are still held by the consumer, instead of waiting. The producer opens the backward FIFO with `O_NONBLOCK`; the producer API returns 3 (`BUFFER_DROPPED`) and a drop counter increments. decimate to delay_sync and both delay_sync outputs run in drop mode. Source: `sh_mem_util.c`, `delay_sync.py`.

**DUMMY frame.** Frame type 1. A header-only frame (`cpi_length = 0`). rtl_daq emits 5 DUMMY frames (`NO_DUMMY_FRAMES`) after every ZMQ command, while the tuners settle. Each command restarts that count at 0, so commands sent back to back share one window of about 5 frames. rebuffer discards its partial CPI on a DUMMY frame. Every DUMMY frame carries `sync_state = 0`. Source: `rtl_daq.c` (`NO_DUMMY_FRAMES`, `fifo_read_tf`), `rebuffer.c`.

**Dwell.** How long the signal scheduler stays on one frequency: `dwell_frames` frames or `dwell_time_sec` seconds per entry (time wins and is converted to frames at load). Source: `signal_scheduler.py`.

**Dynamic range (correlation peak).** The ratio, in dB, of the cross-correlation between a channel and the reference at its peak (or at zero lag once aligned) to its value 100 samples later. delay_sync tests it in every calibration and tracking check: integer-delay calibration, IQ calibration, track lock and tracking, on CAL frames and, in `cal_track_mode = 1`, on live DATA frames. Every channel needs at least 20 dB, or the check fails. The threshold is hardcoded.

The test assumes a sharp, impulse-like correlation peak. A wideband noise signal, such as the calibration noise source, gives one and passes easily. A narrowband signal stays correlated with itself over 100 samples, so its correlation decays slowly and it fails. Source: `delay_sync.py` (`calc_iq_sync`, `min_corr_peak_dyn_range`).

## E {#e}

**Election** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. The leader-selection protocol among coordinator candidates. Candidates poll each other with `LEADER`, ask for votes with `PREVOTE`, and hold leadership through `LEASE` grants. It runs only when `coordinator_candidates` is non-empty. With `require_quorum = 0` (default) two leaders can coexist during a network partition; members then fence the stale one. It is not consensus.

**en_iq_cal.** `[calibration] en_iq_cal`. With 1 (shipped) delay_sync removes the per-channel mean and multiplies each channel by its correction on every outbound frame. With 0 it copies samples unchanged.

**ENGINE.** Make variable that selects the FIR and conversion engine: `auto` (default), `kfr`, `ne10` or `generic`. `auto` picks `kfr` on x86_64 and aarch64, `ne10` on 32-bit ARM, and `generic` elsewhere. `generic` is plain C with no DSP library. Source: `Makefile`.

**Event bus.** The in-process event dispatcher (`daq_events.py`) created when `[monitoring] en_monitoring = 1`. Only delay_sync's bus publishes on port 5003 (two-frame ZMQ messages `[event_type, json]`) and feeds the 5002 `EVENTS` ring. hw_controller's events go only to its log and syslog today. Source: `daq_events.py`, `delay_sync.py`.

**EVENTS, EVENTS_DROPPED.** Port 5002 verbs. `EVENTS` returns up to 100 recent events from delay_sync's ring. `EVENTS_DROPPED` returns how many events the bus dropped because its queue was full.

**Extended ack** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A port 5001 reply that says whether a mutating command was applied: `FNSD` plus `{"applied":true|false|null,"reason":...,"fsm":...,"seq":...}`. A server sends it only on a connection that first sent `XACK`. Other connections get today's bytes.

**External LNA gain.** The gain of an amplifier in front of a receiver, in continuous dB, set in `[amplification] ext_lna_gains_db` or with the `EGAN` verb. It lives in a separate array (`ext_lna_gains_db`). It never goes through the tuner's `valid_gains` table and never enters the header `if_gains`. Header slots 0-31 carry it in tenths of dB. Source: `hw_controller.py`, `gain_budget.py`.

## F {#f}

**Fan-out.** Sending one command to many instances. Today the coordinator fans out `FREQ` and `GAIN` sequentially, with a 5 s timeout per instance. From this release fan-out runs in parallel with one deadline per request.

**Federation.** Running several instances that know about each other. Today it consists of per-instance namespacing (`instance_id`, prefixes, port stride), an optional health thread in delay_sync, and two library-grade services: the coordinator (port 6000) and the IQ router class. Enable the health thread with `[federation] en_federation = 1` and a non-empty `peer_list`. See `scaling_and_clustering.md`.

**Fencing** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. Protection against a deposed coordinator leader. Each member's hw_controller remembers the highest leader term it has seen (`_data_control/<P>fence_term`). It refuses mutating commands that carry a lower, non-zero term (`stale_term`). Direct clients such as heimdall-ctl send term 0 and are never fenced. `daq_stop.sh N --reset-fence` clears the stored term.

**FIR, fir_coeffs.txt.** The decimation low-pass filter. `fir_filter_designer.py` designs it from `fir_tap_size`, `fir_relative_bandwidth` and `fir_window` at every start and writes `_data_control/fir_coeffs.txt`. decimate.out reads it once at init. Today the file is not instance-prefixed, so two instances in one working copy overwrite each other's taps. From this release instance N > 0 uses `_data_control/inst<N>_fir_coeffs.txt` (no key needed).

**FNSD.** The 4-byte prefix of every port 5001 reply ("finished"). A reply is always 128 bytes: `FNSD` plus 124 bytes. For mutating verbs the 124 bytes are zeros. Today this reply is identical for success, an unknown verb, an invalid value and a timed-out request. Source: `hw_controller.py`.

**Follower** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A coordinator candidate that is not the leader. It serves read verbs and answers mutating verbs with `{"ok":false,"error":"not_leader","leader":...}`.

**Forward FIFO.** The named pipe `_data_control/<P>fw_<name>` that carries "segment ready" bytes (and `INIT_READY`, `TERMINATE`) from producer to consumer.

**Fractional delay.** The sub-sample residual timing offset between a channel and the reference after integer alignment. delay_sync estimates it from the phase slope of block FFTs and corrects it with small sample-rate nudges until every channel is within 0.03 samples. Source: `delay_sync.py`.

**Frame.** One unit on the data plane: a 1024-byte IQ header followed by the payload. Before the decimator the payload is interleaved u8 I/Q. After the decimator it is channel-major complex float32 (`data_type = 3`, `sample_bit_depth = 32`).

**Frame period.** `T_fp = Ncpi * R / fs`, the time between DATA frames. 0.437 s at the shipped values (2.29 frames per second).

**Frame types.** The `frame_type` header field:

| Value | Name | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | DATA | normal CPI, decimated |
| 1 | DUMMY | header only, emitted after every tuner command |
| 2 | RAMP | test pattern frame; never reaches consumers through the live chain |
| 3 | CAL | noise source on, `Nc` samples at full ADC rate |
| 4 | TRIGW | trigger-wait frame; never reaches consumers through the live chain |

rebuffer drops any type other than DATA, DUMMY and CAL. Source: `iq_header.h`, `rebuffer.c`.

**FSM (hw_controller).** hw_controller's own state machine. Its states are `STATE_INIT`, `STATE_GAIN_TUNE`, `STATE_GAIN_CTR_WAIT`, `STATE_NOISE_CTR_WAIT` and `STATE_IQ_CAL`. `STATE_IQ_CAL` is the steady state in which mutating control verbs run. Do not confuse it with delay_sync's sync state machine. Source: `hw_controller.py`.

## G {#g}

**Gain (tuner gain).** R820T tuner gain in tenths of dB, for example 297 for 29.7 dB. `[daq] gain`, the `GAIN` verb and the header `if_gains[]` use this unit. Only values in **valid_gains** are accepted.

**Gain lock.** The result of the optional automatic gain search. With `[calibration] en_gain_tune_init = 1`, hw_controller raises all gains one table step per frame until a channel overdrives, backs off one step, and requires `gain_lock_interval` stable frames before it continues. `STATE_GAIN_CTR_WAIT` waits until the header `if_gains` equal the requested values. Source: `hw_controller.py`.

**gen** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A 32-bit schedule generation number that a coordinator puts in each per-member schedule document. A member reports it through the `SCHG` verb, so the coordinator can verify which partition each member runs.

**Generic engine.** `offload_cpu_generic.c`, a dependency-free plain-C FIR engine. Selected at build time with `ENGINE=generic`, or at run time with `[offload] fir_engine = generic` in kfr and ne10 builds.

## H {#h}

**Header (IQ header).** The 1024-byte binary header that starts every frame. It is defined in lockstep in `iq_header.h` and `iq_header.py`, uses native alignment, and is checked by `test_iq_header_abi.py`. Key fields: `sync_word`, `frame_type`, `hardware_id`, `unit_id`, `active_ant_chs`, `rf_center_freq`, `adc_sampling_freq`, `sampling_freq`, `cpi_length`, `time_stamp`, `daq_block_index`, `cpi_index`, `if_gains[32]`, `delay_sync_flag`, `iq_sync_flag`, `sync_state`, `noise_source_state`, `reserved[192]`, `header_version`.

**header_version.** The last header field (offset 1020). rtl_daq stamps 8. Every stage passes it through unchanged and checks only the sync word. The optional HAT bridge sources stamp 7. Source: `iq_header.h`.

**hw_caps.json.** Output of `hw_discover.py`, written to `_data_control/hw_caps.json` at every start. Only `auto_config.py` reads it. It does not detect hardware changes during a run.

**hw_controller.** The Python control stage `hw_controller.py`. It serves port 5001, sends tuner commands to rtl_daq over ZMQ, runs the noise-source policy, the signal scheduler and the orientation controller, and owns the link budget.

**HWSQ** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A port 5001 query verb that returns hw_controller's FSM state, pending request count and frame age from a snapshot. It answers even when frames have stopped.

## I {#i}

**Instance.** One complete DAQ chain (rtl_daq through hw_controller) driving one coherent unit. `[federation] instance_id` identifies it on a host. An instance is the unit of scaling.

**Instance directory** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A per-instance working copy under `<root>/instances/<N>/Firmware` created by `util/provision_instance.py`. Code is symlinked to the install root; `daq_chain_config.ini`, `_data_control/`, `_logs/` and `_db/` are private. Instance 0 runs in `<root>/Firmware`.

**Instance prefix (inst<N>_).** The name prefix that separates the resources of instance N > 0: shared-memory names (`inst2_delay_sync_iq_A`), FIFOs (`_data_control/inst2_fw_delay_sync_iq`) and the control files `iq_track_lock`, `orientation_state` and `bias_tee_state`. Instance 0 uses bare names. Source: `sh_mem_util.c`, `shmemIface.py`.

**instance_registry, instance lock** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. With `[host] instance_registry = 1` the start scripts write a registry record per instance under `$HEIMDALL_RUN_DIR` (default `/run/heimdall`) and hold a per-instance lock. With `[host] instance_guard = refuse` a duplicate start of the same instance is refused. `heimdall-ctl instances` lists the registry.

**iq_server.** `iq_server.out`, the TCP server on port 5000 (+ offset). It runs only when `[data_interface] out_data_iface_type = eth`. It serves one client at a time with a stop-and-wait protocol: the client sends `streaming` once, then `IQDownload` before each next frame. Source: `iq_server.c`.

**iq_track_lock, track-lock intervention.** The control file `_data_control/<P>iq_track_lock`. With `[calibration] require_track_lock_intervention = 1`, hw_controller keeps the noise source on after lock until the file's first byte is `1`. Before this release hw_controller opened this file at init in every configuration and exited if it was missing. From this release `daq_start_sm.sh` creates it containing `0` when it is absent, and hw_controller re-opens it on each check only when the key is 1.

**IQ calibration.** Estimation of each channel's complex gain (amplitude and phase) relative to the reference channel. "IQ" here means the complex (I + jQ) gain of a whole channel. It is not I/Q-imbalance correction inside one receiver, which the chain does not perform.

The method works because, while the noise source is on, all channels receive one common signal. delay_sync forms the channel covariance matrix `Rxx = X X^H` of a CAL frame (`M x M`, one row per channel). One component dominates that matrix, and its eigenvector holds the channels' relative complex gains. delay_sync inverts that eigenvector and normalises it to the reference channel. With the shipped `amplitude_cal_mode = channel_power` only the phase of the result is kept, and the amplitudes come from channel power ratios. The corrections multiply the outbound samples when `en_iq_cal = 1`. Source: `delay_sync.py` (`calc_iq_sync`, `STATE_IQ_CAL`).

**Island.** One coherent unit and its instance. Channels inside an island are coherent. Two islands are never coherent with each other, even on one host, because each unit has its own clock, its own noise source and its own calibration. Islands relate only through the millisecond wall-clock `time_stamp`.

## K {#k}

**KFR.** The C++ DSP library used by the `kfr` FIR engine on x86_64 and aarch64. The build links the copied-in `libkfr_capi.so` with `-rpath $ORIGIN`. Source: `offload_cpu_kfr.c`, `Makefile`.

## L {#l}

**Leader** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. The coordinator candidate that currently holds leadership. Only the leader runs mutating verbs (`FREQ`, `GAIN`, `REBALANCE`, `SCHEDULE SET` and so on). `heimdall-ctl fleet leader` shows it.

**Lease** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A time-limited grant from one candidate to another, sent with `LEASE <term> <endpoint>`. Its length is `election_interval_sec * election_missed_polls` (6 s by default). A leader counts a grant only for slightly less than the lease length, so grants on the two sides never overlap.

**Legacy server, legacy ack** *(term used from this release)*. A port 5001 server that does not understand `XACK` and answers `FNSD` plus zeros. Clients then report the result as "sent, not confirmed" (`applied: null`).

**listen_address.** `[daq] listen_address`, default `0.0.0.0`. It sets the bind address of ports 5000, 5001, 5002 and 5003. It does not affect rtl_daq's ZMQ port 1130, which binds all interfaces unless `[daq] zmq_listen_address` (added in this release) says otherwise. Source: `rtl_daq.c` (`zmq_listen_address`).

**LTO.** Link-time optimisation (`-flto`), enabled in the default `BUILD=release` on x86_64 and aarch64.

## M {#m}

**MARCH.** Make variable for architecture flags. Unset means `-march=native` on x86_64, `-mcpu=native` on aarch64, `-mcpu=cortex-a72 -mtune=cortex-a72` on 32-bit ARM, and no flags elsewhere. `MARCH=portable` drops arch-specific flags for distributable or CI builds. Any other value is passed through.

**Member.** See **cluster member**. A member is managed by a coordinator. A peer is polled by an instance's health thread. One instance can be both.

**METRICS.** A port 5002 verb that returns delay_sync's metric windows (`frame_processing_latency_ms`, `frame_throughput_fps`, per-frame drop deltas) as min, max, avg, p95, count and last over 1000 samples. It requires `[monitoring] en_metrics = 1`. Source: `daq_metrics.py`.

**Mutating verb.** A port 5001 command that changes hardware or schedule state: `FREQ`, `GAIN`, `AGC `, `INIT`, `SCHD`, `SCHS`, `SCHN`, `EGAN`, `BIAS`, `ORNT`, `PARK`, `SCAN`, `OSTP`. hw_controller runs them only in `STATE_IQ_CAL` on a non-dummy frame and defers them otherwise. Compare **query verbs**.

## N {#n}

**Ne10.** The ARM DSP library used by the `ne10` FIR engine on 32-bit ARM. `libNE10.a` is armv7-only, so aarch64 uses KFR.

**Node key** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. The cluster-wide identity of an instance: `host:instance_id`, host in lower case, as written in a membership entry. New coordinator and router tables are keyed by it, because `instance_id` alone repeats across hosts (every host usually runs instance 0).

**node_id** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. `[federation] node_id`, a self-reported label, default `<short hostname>:<instance_id>`. It appears in STATUS, events and `REGISTER`, and as a CRC in header slot 108 when `stamp_node_id = 1`.

**Noise source.** A wideband noise generator inside the unit that feeds the same signal to all channels. Calibration correlates the channels against it. rtl_daq switches it through GPIO 0 of the control channel when `[daq] en_noise_source_ctr = 1`. hw_controller decides when, and only hw_controller sends the command. rtl_daq labels frames CAL whenever the command set the state to on, even when `en_noise_source_ctr = 0` prevents the GPIO write. The noise is injected inside the unit, so calibration cannot see differences in the antenna cables; see **Touchstone**. Source: `rtl_daq.c` (`fifo_read_tf`, noise-source GPIO block in `main`), `hw_controller.py` (`_control_noise_source`).

**Noise burst.** A period with the noise source on. hw_controller turns it on whenever `sync_state < 5` and, in tracking mode 2, periodically after `cal_frame_interval` frames. Each switch costs about 5 DUMMY frames: hw_controller sends the gain command and the noise-source command back to back, and the second command restarts the same 5-frame window. The burst replaces DATA with CAL frames. At the shipped values a periodic burst loses about 2.4 to 2.6 s of samples and leaves a 2.9 to 3.1 s gap between DATA frames (derived from the code; see the FAQ "How often does the chain recalibrate").

**noise_source_state.** Header field: 1 while the noise source is commanded on. Such frames are CAL frames.

## O {#o}

**Offload engine.** The pluggable FIR implementation behind `fir_engine_create()` (`offload.h`): `kfr`, `neon`, `generic`, `fpga`, `gpu`. `[offload] fir_engine` selects it at run time among the engines compiled in. The FPGA and GPU engines are experimental and are not exercised at the shipped `R = 1`.

**Orientation controller.** The optional rotator or pan-tilt control in hw_controller (`[orientation]`). Backends are `mock`, `gs232`, `pwm_servo` and `i2c_pantilt`. Verbs are `ORNT`, `SCAN`, `PARK`, `OSTP` and `OQRY`. Motion waits until `sync_state >= min_sync_state` and the noise source is off.

**Overrun (USB ring-buffer overrun).** rtl_daq keeps a ring of `[daq] usb_ring_buffers` blocks per channel (default 8, allowed 2 to 64; the key is added in this release). When a channel's USB reader gets that many blocks ahead of frame assembly, rtl_daq counts an overrun, still emits the frame, and stamps the cumulative count in reserved slot 102. Its warning suggests raising `usb_ring_buffers`. Frames emitted during an overrun have no coherence guarantee. Today no stage reads slot 102. Source: `rtl_daq.c` (`num_buff`, overrun block in the main loop).

## P {#p}

**P1dB.** The 1 dB compression point: the output power at which an amplifier's gain has dropped 1 dB below its small-signal value. `[amplification] ext_lna_p1db_dbm` sets it per channel (99 means "not modelled"). The link budget warns when the estimated output level (from `expected_input_dbm`, see **compression flags**) comes within `p1db_margin_db` of it.

**Partition strategy.** How the federation scheduler splits a master frequency list across instances: `round_robin` (interleaved) or `range` (contiguous blocks). Any other name falls back to `round_robin`. Source: `federation_scheduler.py`.

**Peer, peer_list.** `[federation] peer_list` lists the other instances that this instance's health thread polls, as `host:instance_id` (a number of 1024 or more is read as a legacy status port). The thread runs inside delay_sync only when `en_federation = 1` and the list is non-empty. It polls each peer's port 5002 `STATUS` every 5 s. Source: `federation_health.py`.

**PGO.** Profile-guided optimisation. `make pgo-profile` builds instrumented binaries, a run collects `.gcda` profiles, and `make pgo-optimize` rebuilds with `-fprofile-use`. `make clean` keeps the profiles; `make distclean` removes them.

**Pipeline health.** The `pipeline_health` field of port 5002 STATUS: `ok` when `sync_state >= 5` and no drops in the last `drop_window_sec` (default 60 s), `degraded` when `sync_state >= 2`, otherwise `error`. It counts only drops on delay_sync's two outputs. Source: `daq_status_server.py`.

**Port stride, port offset.** Every per-instance port is `base + instance_id * port_stride` (`compute_port`). `[federation] port_stride` defaults to 100. The coordinator (6000) and the router (7000) are not offset. Source: `sh_mem_util.c`.

**Preflight** *(opt-in, planned in this release; `daq_preflight.py` is not in the tree yet)*. `Firmware/daq_preflight.py` checks cores, memory, `/dev/shm`, USB bus budget, ports and limits against one or more configs before you start. `[host] preflight = warn|strict` runs it from the start script; `heimdall-ctl capacity` wraps it.

## Q {#q}

**Query verbs.** The port 5001 verbs that only read state: `RFQ ` (link budget), `OQRY` (orientation) and `SCHQ` (scheduler). They reply `FNSD` plus NUL-padded JSON and are answered in any FSM state, but only while frames arrive. With no frames, the reply after 10 s is `FNSD{"error":"busy"}`. Source: `hw_controller.py` (`QUERY_COMMANDS`, `_submit_request`).

**Quorum** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. With `[federation] require_quorum = 1`, a coordinator leader needs unexpired leases from a majority of candidates, and mutating verbs fail with `no_quorum` without one. Quorum needs at least 3 candidates to be useful.

## R {#r}

**RAMP frame.** Frame type 2, a test-pattern frame. The live chain never forwards it.

**Rate nudge (sample-frequency correction).** The ZMQ `s` command. It changes the sample rate of one or more channels by a small fractional offset for one DAQ block, then restores the nominal rate. The rate is set by the RTL2832U demodulator's digital resampler, not by the R820T tuner, which only does RF gain and mixing. During that block the nudged channels' streams slip by roughly `offset * B` samples relative to the others. delay_sync uses this to remove integer and fractional delays in the hardware.

The offsets are fractions, not ppm, despite the "ppm" naming in delay_sync: 0.008 means 0.8 %. An offset of 0.008 or more (`FS_CORRECTION_KEEP_LIMIT`) is left applied after the block. That channel then keeps slipping until the next `s` command. Source: `rtl_daq.c` (`fifo_read_tf`, `FS_CORRECTION_KEEP_LIMIT`, sample-rate correction in the main loop).

**rebalance (REBALANCE).** The coordinator verb that repartitions a master schedule across instances and sends each instance its part. Today the shipped coordinator has no way to set a master schedule, so REBALANCE sends nothing and still replies `{"status":"rebalanced",...}`. From this release `SCHEDULE SET` sets the master schedule, and REBALANCE without one replies `{"error":"no master schedule"}`.

**rebuffer.** `rebuffer.out`, the stage that reshapes DAQ blocks from rtl_daq's stdout into CPI-sized DATA frames and `Nc`-sized CAL frames, and writes them to the `decimator_in` shared-memory hop.

**RECL, recal** *(RECL is opt-in, added in this release)*. `heimdall-ctl recal` sends `INIT` today, which only re-enters hw_controller's `STATE_INIT`. It does not make a locked delay_sync recalibrate. With `[calibration] en_wire_recal = 1`, the new `RECL` verb makes delay_sync restart calibration.

**Reconciliation** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. With `reconcile_assignments` enabled, the coordinator leader periodically checks each member's schedule generation and re-sends or stops schedules so members converge to the recorded assignment.

**Reference channel (std_ch_ind).** `[calibration] std_ch_ind`, the channel all others are aligned and corrected against (shipped 0). Its correction is fixed at 1.

**REGISTER** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A coordinator verb that an instance sends every `register_interval_sec` when `[federation] register_with_coordinator = 1`. It adds the instance to the membership without editing the coordinator's config.

**Reserved slots.** The 192 `uint32` words of `reserved[]` at header offset 252. Slot `k` is at byte `252 + 4k`. Unstamped slots are 0, and there are no presence bits.

| Slots | Content | Written when |
|---|---|---|
| 0-31 | external LNA gain, dB x10 | `[amplification]` enabled |
| 32-63 | total system gain, dB x10 | `[amplification]` enabled |
| 64-95 | system noise figure, milli-dB | `[amplification]` enabled |
| 96 | compression flags | `[amplification]` enabled |
| 97 | bias-tee bitmask | `[amplification]` enabled |
| 98, 99 | antenna azimuth, elevation in centi-degrees (elevation +9000 offset) | `en_orientation = 1` |
| 100 | rotator state (0-3) | `en_orientation = 1` |
| 101 | aggregate channel power, milli-dB, signed | front-end telemetry enabled; computed on DATA frames, repeated on every frame |
| 102 | cumulative USB overrun count | always, by rtl_daq |
| 103-105 | router sequence and receive time | router `--stamp-seq`, `--stamp-rx-ts` (this release) |
| 106-107 | source instance + 1, CRC32 of source node key | router `--tag-mode node` (this release) |
| 108 | CRC32 of `node_id` | `[federation] stamp_node_id = 1` (this release) |
| 109 | decimator drop count | `[monitoring] stamp_decimator_drops = 1` (this release) |
| 110-113 | calibration quality (slot 110, milli-dB, signed) and counters | `[monitoring] stamp_cal_telemetry = 1` (this release) |

"Signed" slots hold a signed int32 in two's complement. The `iq_header.py` accessors sign-extend slots 0-95, 98-99, 101 and 110. A consumer that reads them as `uint32` sees values near 4.29e9 for negative numbers. Source: `iq_header.h`, `iq_header.py` (`_sx32`).

**Router (IQ router).** `federation_iq_router.py`. Today it is a library class with no command-line entry: it connects to each instance's port 5000 as a normal client, overwrites `unit_id` with the source `instance_id`, and forwards every frame to every client of one output port (7000) in arrival order. From this release it has a CLI, bounded per-client queues, a stats port (7001), tag modes, loss detection and optional time alignment.

**rtl_daq.** `rtl_daq.out`, the acquisition stage. It opens one RTL-SDR per channel, reads USB blocks with one thread per channel, assembles one frame per block, serves ZMQ tuner commands on port 1130 (+ offset), and writes frames to stdout.

## S {#s}

**Safe state.** `STATE_IQ_CAL` of hw_controller on a non-dummy frame: the only moment mutating control verbs execute.

**Sample delay (integer delay).** The whole-sample offset of a channel relative to the reference, found from the peak of a cross-correlation of CAL frames. It arises because each dongle starts streaming independently.

**Schedule (signal scheduler).** `signal_scheduler.py`, a frequency-hopping list run by hw_controller (`[schedule]`, or the `SCHD` verb with JSON or a file path). `repeat_mode` is `loop`, `once` or `pingpong`. With `require_cal_on_hop = 1` it waits for `sync_state >= 6` after each hop, up to `max_cal_wait_frames`.

**set_unit_serials.sh** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. `util/set_unit_serials.sh` reprograms one KrakenSDR's five EEPROM serials to `1000 + 100*K + i` for unit K, so several units can coexist on one host.

**Shared-memory output (shmem) vs eth.** `[data_interface] out_data_iface_type`. `shmem` (shipped) means your DSP application attaches to the `delay_sync_iq` ring on the same host and no iq_server runs. `eth` starts iq_server on port 5000. When the key is absent, the start script assumes `eth`.

**Status server.** The port 5002 JSON server (`daq_status_server.py`) inside delay_sync, enabled by `[monitoring] en_status_server = 1`. The `[monitoring]` section must exist. `en_monitoring` is not required, but without it `EVENTS` and `EVENTS_DROPPED` return `event bus not enabled`. One text command per connection, one JSON line back. Verbs: `PING`, `STATUS`, `METRICS`, `EVENTS`, `EVENTS_DROPPED`, and with `[database]` enabled `DB_STATS`, `SCAN_SUMMARY`, `CAL_HISTORY`. At most 8 concurrent clients.

**Supervisor** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. `Firmware/daq_supervise.sh` starts one instance, watches its PID files (and optionally its STATUS), and stops only that instance when a stage dies. The supervised systemd units use it.

**sync_state.** The header field that reports delay_sync's calibration progress:

| sync_state | delay_sync state(s) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | none | before the first frame, and on every DUMMY frame |
| 1 | `STATE_INIT` | waiting for the first CAL frame |
| 2 | `STATE_SAMPLE_CAL` | measuring integer delays |
| 3 | `STATE_SYNC_WAIT`, `STATE_FRAC_SAMPLE_CAL`, `STATE_FRAC_SYNC_WAIT` | waiting for a nudge to take effect, or measuring fractional delays |
| 4 | `STATE_IQ_CAL` | correcting amplitude and phase |
| 5 | `STATE_TRACK_LOCK` | locked, waiting for the noise source to turn off |
| 6 | `STATE_TRACK` | tracking on live data |

Three internal states share the value 3. Source: `delay_sync.py`.

**Sync word.** `0x2bf7b95a`, the first header field. Every stage validates it; it is the only header check stages make.

**Synthetic mode.** Running the chain without hardware: `daq_synthetic_start.sh` replaces rtl_daq with `_testing/test_data_synthesizer.py`, which generates delayed, phase-shifted copies of one noise signal per channel.

## T {#t}

**Tag mode** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. The router's `--tag-mode`: `instance` (default, today's behaviour) overwrites header `unit_id` with the source `instance_id`; `unit` leaves `unit_id` alone; `node` leaves it alone and stamps slots 106 and 107 so frames can be attributed by node key.

**Term** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A monotonically increasing 32-bit election epoch. A candidate increments it when it claims leadership and persists it before sending it. Members use the highest term seen for fencing.

**time_stamp.** Header field: milliseconds since the Unix epoch from `gettimeofday()` on the acquiring host, taken when the last block of the frame completed on all channels and back-dated by rebuffer for queued samples. It is wall-clock time, not monotonic, and has no PPS, GPS or PTP input. Source: `rtl_daq.c` (`gettimeofday` in the main loop), `rebuffer.c`.

**Touchstone, iq_adjust.** Touchstone is a file format for measured network parameters. It is one source of the `iq_adjust` cable correction.

The noise source is injected inside the unit, so calibration aligns the channels only from the injection point inward. Phase and amplitude differences in the antenna cables are outside the calibration loop. `[calibration] iq_adjust_source` adds a fixed per-channel correction for them:

| `iq_adjust_source` | Correction |
|---|---|
| `explicit-time-delay` (shipped) | `iq_adjust_time_delay_ns` becomes a phase at the centre frequency (`2*pi*f*tau`), plus `iq_adjust_amplitude` in dB. Both lists have one value per non-reference channel (`M - 1` values). |
| `touchstone` | delay_sync reads `_calibration/cable_ch{m}.s1p` and uses its single S-parameter as the cable's transmission response at the frequency point nearest the RF centre frequency, normalised to the reference channel. |

Store the measured S21 (transmission) of each cable in the `.s1p` file, not a reflection (S11) measurement. The code reads the file's only parameter as a through response, so an S11 file gives wrong corrections. Source: `delay_sync.py` (`iq_adjust` setup in the config reader).

**Track lock.** `STATE_TRACK_LOCK` (`sync_state = 5`): calibration has converged. hw_controller then turns the noise source off and delay_sync enters `STATE_TRACK` on the first DATA frame.

**Tracking.** `STATE_TRACK` (`sync_state = 6`). delay_sync watches for drift according to `cal_track_mode`. A failure counter goes up on a failed check, down on a passed one (never below 0), and back to 0 on every DUMMY frame. When it reaches `maximum_sync_fails`, or on any change of `rf_center_freq`, delay_sync returns to `STATE_INIT`. In mode 2 every burst starts with DUMMY frames, so the failures must occur within one burst. At the shipped values (`maximum_sync_fails = 10`, `cal_frame_burst_size = 10`) nearly every CAL frame of one burst must fail.

**Transport.** The C data-plane abstraction (`transport.h`). `shm` wraps the shared-memory hop and is the only backend that works end to end. The `spi`, `pcie`, `usb3` and `net` drivers are compiled out by default, and their Python counterparts are stubs.

**TRIGW frame.** Frame type 4, a trigger-wait frame. The live chain never forwards it.

## U {#u}

**unified_gain_control.** `[calibration] unified_gain_control = 1` forces all channels to the lowest requested gain index.

**unit_id.** Header field identifying the physical unit, from `[hw] unit_id` (default 0). It is not derived from `instance_id` today. The router overwrites it with the source `instance_id` in its default mode. From this release `[hw] unit_id = auto` stamps `instance_id` at the source.

## V {#v}

**valid_gains.** The 29 tuner gain steps hw_controller accepts, in tenths of dB: 0, 9, 14, 27, 37, 77, 87, 125, 144, 157, 166, 197, 207, 229, 254, 280, 297, 328, 338, 364, 372, 386, 402, 421, 434, 439, 445, 480, 496. A `GAIN` value outside this list is logged at ERROR and answered `range`, but it is not fully ignored: the gains of the channels before the bad value are already stored (in `last_gains` during a burst) and take effect at the next gain change or burst restore. Send a complete, valid list to recover. Source: `hw_controller.py` (`_handle_control_reqest`).

## X {#x}

**XACK** *(opt-in, added in this release)*. A port 5001 handshake verb. A client sends `XACK` with its term and cluster id before a command. A new server replies with JSON (`xack`, channel count, capabilities, timeouts) and then sends extended acks on that connection. An old server replies `FNSD` plus zeros and logs `Unidentified control command: XACK` once per connection; that log line is expected in mixed-version clusters. It appears only at `[daq] log_level` 4 or lower (see "Which log lines appear at the shipped log level?"). The coordinator always sends XACK first, so it never sends a command into a connection that is still queued behind another client.

## Z {#z}

**ZMQ control link (port 1130).** The internal REQ/REP link from delay_sync and hw_controller to rtl_daq, on `1130 + <off>`. Messages are 128 bytes: a module id byte, a command character (`r`, `c`, `g`, `a`, `s`, `n`, `b`, `h`) and a payload. rtl_daq replies `ok` to any command and then emits 5 DUMMY frames. It binds all interfaces by default and has no authentication. Do not expose it. Source: `inter_module_messages.py`, `rtl_daq.c` (`fifo_read_tf`).

---

# Part 2: FAQ {#part-2-faq}

## Getting started {#getting-started}

### How do I run the chain without hardware? {#how-do-i-run-the-chain-without-hardware}

Use the hardware-free test suite first. It needs no sudo, no SDR and no compiled binaries, and it runs on Linux and macOS:

```bash
cd Firmware
./unit_test.sh --ci
python3 ini_checker.py daq_chain_config.ini no_hw
```

For a running simulated chain, use the synthetic start script after `make` in `Firmware/_daq_core`:

```bash
cd Firmware
sudo ./daq_synthetic_start.sh
sudo ./daq_stop.sh
```

**Today** the synthetic chain does not work out of the box. The synthesizer opens `_data_control/rec_control_fifo` for reading at import time, and no script creates that path. If it is missing, the synthesizer exits with an error before it generates any data. If you create it with `mkfifo`, the open blocks until something opens it for writing, and nothing in the repository does. The synthesizer also has no ZMQ socket on port 1130, so hw_controller's gain and noise-source commands time out, and CAL frames appear only when the FIFO protocol turns the noise source on. Source: `test_data_synthesizer.py` and `daq_synthetic_start.sh` in the revision before this release.

**From this release:** the synthesizer answers ZMQ commands on `1130 + <off>` like rtl_daq, models the `s` rate nudge, and the simulated chain can reach lock. This is a default-path fix; no key is needed.

### What must be attached for the chain to run? {#what-must-be-attached-for-the-chain-to-run}

With the shipped `out_data_iface_type = shmem`, a consumer application must attach to the `delay_sync_iq` shared-memory ring. Until one does, delay_sync waits in its output setup, as explained in the next answer. With `eth`, iq_server runs and the chain flows without a client, but output frames are dropped until one connects.

### Why does the chain stop if nothing reads the shared-memory output? {#why-does-the-chain-stop-if-nothing-reads-the-shared-memory-output}

Because delay_sync opens its output producer with a blocking FIFO open. The open returns only when a consumer opens the other end.

The sequence in `delay_sync.py` is:

1. delay_sync attaches to its input, `decimator_out`.
2. It creates `delay_sync_iq` and opens `_data_control/<P>fw_delay_sync_iq` for writing. This blocks until a reader opens the FIFO.
3. Only then does it create `delay_sync_hwc`, the ring that feeds hw_controller, and start the status server and federation health thread.

While delay_sync waits:

- decimate.out keeps running and drops every frame at `decimator_out`, because that hop is in drop mode.
- hw_controller receives no frames, so it executes no control request. Its port 5001 server still accepts connections. After 10 s it replies `FNSD` plus zeros to a mutating verb (the command was cancelled, not applied) and `FNSD{"error":"busy"}` to a query verb.
- Port 5002 is not listening yet.

Once your consumer attaches, the delay_sync outputs run in drop mode: a slow consumer causes dropped frames, not a stall. Attach your consumer as part of your start procedure. `Firmware/_testing/unit_test/capture_shmem_stream.py` is an in-tree consumer example for instance 0. See `consumer_guide.md`.

### Why does STATUS say "degraded" when no client is connected? {#why-does-status-say-degraded-when-no-client-is-connected}

Because frames are being dropped toward the absent consumer. `pipeline_health` is `ok` only when `sync_state >= 5` and there were no drops on delay_sync's outputs in the last `drop_window_sec` (60 s by default).

In `eth` mode iq_server consumes the ring only during a client session. With no client, delay_sync finds both segments busy and drops every frame. `counters.dropped_frames_iq` grows and health becomes `degraded` even with a perfect lock. Connect a client, or read `sync_state` and `calibration_status` instead of `pipeline_health`. Source: `delay_sync.py`, `daq_status_server.py`.

### Where are the logs? {#where-are-the-logs}

In `Firmware/_logs/` for instance 0 and `Firmware/_logs/inst<N>/` for instance N > 0. Older logs move to `<log dir>/archive/<date>/` at each start, keeping the last 10.

| File | Written by |
|---|---|
| `rtl_daq.log` | rtl_daq.out (hardware mode) |
| `synthetic.log` | the synthesizer (synthetic mode) |
| `rebuffer.log` | rebuffer.out |
| `decimator.log` | decimate.out |
| `delay_sync.log` | delay_sync.py, including the status server and federation health |
| `hwc.log` | hw_controller.py |
| `iq_server.log` | iq_server.out (`eth` mode only) |

PID files live in `_logs/inst<N>/pids/`, also for instance 0 (`_logs/inst0/pids/`). See `operations_runbook.md`.

### Which log lines appear at the shipped log level? {#which-log-lines-appear-at-the-shipped-log-level}

Only fatal and critical ones. The shipped config sets `[daq] log_level = 5`, which hides almost every line that the answers below tell you to look for.

`[daq] log_level` uses one scale for every stage:

| `log_level` | Python stages (delay_sync, hw_controller, the 5001 server) | C stages (rtl_daq, rebuffer, decimate, iq_server) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | DEBUG | DEBUG |
| 2 | INFO | INFO |
| 3 | WARNING | WARN |
| 4 | ERROR | ERROR |
| 5 (shipped) | CRITICAL | FATAL |

The Python stages multiply the value by 10 and pass it to `logging`; the C stages pass it to `log_set_level()` in `log.c`. These lines are hidden at the shipped value 5:

| Line | Level | Logged by |
|---|---|---|
| `Improper gain value`, `Unidentified control command`, `Failed to load schedule` | ERROR | hw_controller |
| `Correlation peak dynamic range is insufficient to perform calibration` | WARNING | delay_sync |
| `Fractional delays:`, `Sending ppm offsets:`, per-channel `Peak dyn. range:` | DEBUG | delay_sync |
| `Sampling frequency correction set` | INFO | rtl_daq |

To see them, set `log_level = 1` for the debug lines, or at most 4 for the error lines, then restart the chain:

```ini
[daq]
log_level = 1
```

Source: `delay_sync.py` and `hw_controller.py` (`log_level * 10`), `rtl_daq.c` (`log_set_level`), `log.h`.

## Calibration and sync {#calibration-and-sync}

### Why is my sync_state stuck at 3? {#why-is-my-sync_state-stuck-at-3}

Because delay_sync is either waiting for a rate nudge to take effect or cannot get the fractional delay below 0.03 samples. Three internal states report 3, so the header alone cannot tell you which.

| State behind the 3 | Leaves when | Usual cause of a hang |
|---|---|---|
| `STATE_SYNC_WAIT` | the first DUMMY frame after an integer-delay nudge arrives | the DUMMY frames that follow the nudge did not reach delay_sync. The `decimator_out` hop is in drop mode, so it can drop them while delay_sync is busy. |
| `STATE_FRAC_SAMPLE_CAL` | every channel's fractional delay is within 0.03 samples | weak or missing noise signal on a channel, a bad cable or connector, or a channel whose estimate keeps oscillating |
| `STATE_FRAC_SYNC_WAIT` | the first DUMMY frame after a fractional nudge | as for `STATE_SYNC_WAIT` |

delay_sync enters a wait state only after rtl_daq has replied `ok` to the `s` command. rtl_daq emits 5 DUMMY frames after every command it acknowledges. An unanswered command (5 s ZMQ timeout) keeps delay_sync in the measuring state, where it retries; see the sync_state 2 answer.

Check `delay_sync.log` for `Fractional delays:` and `Sending ppm offsets:` lines, and `rtl_daq.log` for `Sampling frequency correction set`. Both need a lower `[daq] log_level` than shipped; see "Which log lines appear at the shipped log level?". Source: `delay_sync.py` (`STATE_SAMPLE_CAL` through `STATE_FRAC_SYNC_WAIT`, `_rtl_daq_transaction`).

**From this release:** with `[monitoring] status_extended = 1`, STATUS adds `fsm_state`, which names the exact delay_sync state.

### What do sync_state 1 and 2 hangs mean? {#what-do-sync_state-1-and-2-hangs-mean}

`sync_state = 1` means delay_sync has seen no CAL frame. It leaves `STATE_INIT` only on a CAL frame, and only hw_controller's `n` command makes rtl_daq label frames CAL. Check that hw_controller is running, and that it is not stuck before its `STATE_IQ_CAL` (see `hwc.log`).

`sync_state = 2` has two causes:

- CAL frames arrive, but the correlation peak is below the 20 dB dynamic-range limit on some channel. Typical causes are the noise source not reaching that channel, a dead dongle, or heavy interference. Check `[daq] en_noise_source_ctr = 1`. With 0, rtl_daq still labels frames CAL but never switches the noise source, so no common signal reaches the channels.
- The `s` nudge is never acknowledged. delay_sync waits up to 5 s for rtl_daq's reply on port 1130, then stays in `STATE_SAMPLE_CAL` and retries. This happens when rtl_daq has died, and in synthetic mode today, where nothing answers port 1130 at all.

delay_sync logs `Correlation peak dynamic range is insufficient to perform calibration` for the first cause, but only below the shipped log level; see "Which log lines appear at the shipped log level?". If dynamic range drops during IQ calibration, the state also falls back from 4 to 2.

### Why does "heimdall-ctl recal" not recalibrate? {#why-does-heimdall-ctl-recal-not-recalibrate}

Because it sends `INIT`, and `INIT` only resets hw_controller. hw_controller re-enters its `STATE_INIT`, re-sends its current gains (not the config file values) and turns the noise source off. Nothing in that path tells a locked delay_sync to start over. Source: `hw_controller.py` (`STATE_INIT`), `delay_sync.py` (`STATE_TRACK`).

What does trigger recalibration today:

- a frequency change (`FREQ`, `heimdall-ctl tune`, or a scheduler hop), because delay_sync returns to `STATE_INIT` whenever `rf_center_freq` changes;
- drift: `maximum_sync_fails` failed checks (net of passed ones) during tracking. The counter resets on every DUMMY frame, so in mode 2 they must fall within one burst; see **Tracking**.

A workaround is to retune to a different frequency and back.

**From this release:** set `[calibration] en_wire_recal = 1`, then send `RECL` (`heimdall-ctl` and the coordinator's `RECAL` use it). delay_sync restarts calibration from `STATE_INIT`.

### How often does the chain recalibrate, and how much data does it lose? {#how-often-does-the-chain-recalibrate-and-how-much-data-does-it-lose}

With the shipped `cal_track_mode = 2`, `cal_frame_interval = 687` and `cal_frame_burst_size = 10`:

| Quantity | Value at shipped settings |
|---|---|
| Interval between bursts | 687 frames, about 300 s |
| Burst length | at least 11 CAL frames at block rate (one per 109.2 ms block), about 1.2 s. The first CAL frame only ends hw_controller's wait state and is not counted; the 10th counted frame switches the noise off |
| Total data outage per burst | about 22 to 24 blocks: 5 DUMMY + at least 11 CAL + 5 DUMMY, plus the 1 or 2 blocks of the partial CPI rebuffer discards. That is 2.4 to 2.6 s of lost samples and a 2.9 to 3.1 s gap between DATA frames |
| Duty cycle lost | about 0.8 to 0.9 % |

These figures are derived from the code (`hw_controller.py` burst counter, `rebuffer.c`), not measured. To measure, log `frame_type` and `time_stamp` across one burst.

A retune always costs a full calibration on top of that. Source: `hw_controller.py`.

### Does changing the gain trigger recalibration? {#does-changing-the-gain-trigger-recalibration}

No. Calibration is measured at a fixed gain from the calibration gain table, not at your operating gain. hw_controller sets that gain for each burst and restores your gains afterwards. A `GAIN` command while the noise source is on only updates the saved gains. Gain changes do not move delay_sync out of tracking. Source: `hw_controller.py` (`_control_noise_source`).

The corrections assume that inter-channel amplitude and phase do not depend on gain. Calibration runs with every channel at the same gain, and delay_sync applies the same corrections to every outbound frame. If you set different gains per channel, the outbound amplitudes differ by those gain differences. Any gain-dependent phase difference between tuners is not corrected either. Mode 2 re-checks only CAL frames, which are taken at the calibration gain, so it never detects this mismatch. The shipped config allows per-channel gains (`unified_gain_control = 0`). For direction finding, keep all channels at the same gain: set `[calibration] unified_gain_control = 1`, or give one value in `[daq] gain`.

### Why are the sync flags 1 on frames that were never checked? {#why-are-the-sync-flags-1-on-frames-that-were-never-checked}

In `cal_track_mode` 0 and 2, delay_sync sets `delay_sync_flag` and `iq_sync_flag` to 1 on DATA frames in `STATE_TRACK` without a measurement.

In mode 2 only CAL frames are checked, so only CAL frames can carry a 0 flag. DATA frames always carry 1. A consumer that skips CAL frames and reads the flags on DATA frames never sees a failed check. The failure counter goes up on a failed check, down on a passed one, and back to 0 on every DUMMY frame, that is, at every burst. At the shipped values (`maximum_sync_fails = 10`, `cal_frame_burst_size = 10`) every CAL frame of one burst must fail before delay_sync recalibrates.

Mode 1 checks every DATA frame, but on live data. It compares each frame's inter-channel phase and amplitude pattern with the pattern on the first DATA frame after lock, and it requires a sharp correlation peak (20 dB at a 100-sample lag). That works only while one strong, wideband, stationary signal is present. A moving source, a changing scene, a narrowband signal or no signal at all count as sync failures and trigger recalibration, with the data loss of a full calibration each time. Most deployments should keep mode 2 and read CAL-frame flags or `sync_state` to judge calibration health. Source: `delay_sync.py` (`STATE_TRACK_LOCK`, `STATE_TRACK`, DUMMY handling).

### Why do I see five header-only frames after every command? {#why-do-i-see-five-header-only-frames-after-every-command}

rtl_daq emits 5 DUMMY frames after every ZMQ command, whatever the command, while tuners settle. rebuffer also discards the partial CPI. At the shipped block period that is about 0.55 s of dead time per command, plus up to 0.33 s of discarded CPI. Commands sent back to back share one window, because each command restarts the 5-frame count instead of adding another. A frequency hop or a burst switch (gain plus noise source) therefore costs about 5 DUMMY frames, and a full periodic burst costs two such windows, one when the noise source turns on and one when it turns off.

## Control and monitoring {#control-and-monitoring}

### My control command was acknowledged but nothing happened. Why? {#my-control-command-was-acknowledged-but-nothing-happened-why}

Today every mutating port 5001 command gets `FNSD` plus zeros. That reply is identical for success and for these failures:

| Cause | What happened |
|---|---|
| hw_controller not in `STATE_IQ_CAL` | the command waits; after 10 s the server gives up and the request is cancelled |
| request queue full (8 pending) | the request is dropped |
| unknown verb | logged, ignored |
| `GAIN` value not in `valid_gains` | logged at ERROR, reply `range`; gains of the channels before the bad value are still stored and applied later |
| `GAIN` list shorter than `num_ch` | the missing channels get gain 0, because 0 is a valid gain |
| `SCHD` JSON or file that fails to load | logged, ignored |
| `INIT` during a noise burst | deferred until the burst ends |

Read `hwc.log` to see what happened. The "logged" lines are at ERROR level, so they appear only with `[daq] log_level` 4 or lower; the shipped 5 hides them. See "Which log lines appear at the shipped log level?". Source: `hw_controller.py` (`_handle_control_reqest`, `_submit_request`).

**From this release:** a client that sends `XACK` first gets an extended ack with `applied` and a `reason` such as `ok`, `range`, `queue_full`, `deferred_timeout`, `held_for_burst` or `not_confirmed`. heimdall-ctl and the coordinator do this automatically and report the outcome.

### Why does "heimdall-ctl tune" print success even when nothing changed? {#why-does-heimdall-ctl-tune-print-success-even-when-nothing-changed}

Today `tune`, `gain`, `agc`, `recal` and `schedule load|stop|next` discard the server's reply and print a success message unconditionally. Only `orientation`, `rf-budget` and `schedule query` get data back, because they send query verbs. `lna-gain`, `bias-tee`, `bearing`, `park` and `scan` send mutating verbs (`EGAN`, `BIAS`, `ORNT`, `PARK`, `SCAN`/`OSTP`). They pass the reply to `_print_ctl_reply`, but a mutating verb's reply is `FNSD` plus zeros, so they also print their success text for any `FNSD` reply. Source: `util/heimdall_ctl/__main__.py` (`_print_ctl_reply`).

**From this release:** mutating subcommands read and report the reply. Against an old server they print that the server does not confirm application. Socket errors print `Error: ...` and exit 3 instead of a traceback.

### Why does port 5001 not answer, or answer only after 10 s? {#why-does-port-5001-not-answer-or-answer-only-after-10-s}

Check these in order:

1. hw_controller is not running. Look at `hwc.log`. Before this release, for an instance N > 0, a missing `_data_control/inst<N>_iq_track_lock` made `init()` fail and the process exit; create the file with `printf 0 > _data_control/inst<N>_iq_track_lock`. **From this release** `daq_start_sm.sh` creates it, and hw_controller reads it only when `require_track_lock_intervention = 1`.
2. No frames reach hw_controller, for example in a shmem chain with no consumer attached (see the shared-memory question above). The server still accepts the connection, because hw_controller starts it before it waits for frames. After 10 s it replies `FNSD` plus zeros to a mutating verb (the command was cancelled, not applied) and `FNSD{"error":"busy"}` to a query. The zero reply looks like success.
3. Another client holds the connection. The port 5001 server serves one TCP connection at a time until that client disconnects. A resident DoA application that keeps its connection open blocks every other client. **From this release** `[daq] ctl_max_connections = 4` serves several connections.

### What changes if I enable [monitoring]? {#what-changes-if-i-enable-monitoring}

Nothing on the data path. `[monitoring] en_monitoring = 1` creates the event buses. Each sub-feature has its own switch. Some need `en_monitoring = 1` and some need only the section to exist.

These keys work without `en_monitoring`:

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `en_status_server = 1` | port 5002 (+ offset) JSON server inside delay_sync; `EVENTS` and `EVENTS_DROPPED` then return `event bus not enabled` |
| `en_metrics = 1` | latency and throughput windows in `METRICS` and STATUS |
| `heartbeat_interval` | frames between heartbeat events and STATUS refreshes (default 100) |

These keys take effect only with `en_monitoring = 1`:

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `en_zmq_pub = 1` | port 5003 (+ offset) ZMQ PUB of delay_sync's events |
| `en_syslog = 1` | events to syslog (`syslog_address`, `syslog_min_severity`) |
| `event_ring_size` | events kept for the `EVENTS` verb (default 500) |

Source: `delay_sync.py` (`[monitoring]` block of the config reader).

Points to know:

- The STATUS snapshot refreshes only every `heartbeat_interval` frames, about 44 s at the shipped settings. With `heartbeat_interval = 0` it never refreshes.
- A bind failure on 5002 is only logged; the chain keeps running.
- Only delay_sync's events reach 5003 and `EVENTS`. hw_controller events (gain, noise source, orientation, schedule) go only to `hwc.log` and syslog.

**From this release:** `status_update_interval` refreshes the snapshot independently, `status_extended = 1` adds identity, configuration and freshness fields plus a `stale` health value, and `en_hwc_state_relay = 1` relays hw_controller's state and events through delay_sync to 5002 and 5003.

### Why does "heimdall-ctl events --tail" show nothing useful? {#why-does-heimdall-ctl-events---tail-show-nothing-useful}

Today the subscriber reads one ZMQ frame and splits it at the first space, but the publisher sends two frames: the topic, then the JSON. The tail mode therefore misparses messages. Use `heimdall-ctl events` (without `--tail`), which reads the 5002 `EVENTS` ring. **From this release** `--tail` decodes the two-frame messages. Source: `util/heimdall_ctl/client/events_sub.py`, `daq_events.py`.

### Does heimdall-ctl work against a remote host or another instance? {#does-heimdall-ctl-work-against-a-remote-host-or-another-instance}

Partly. `--host` and `--instance N` change the target address and add `N * port_stride` to ports 5001, 5002 and 5003. Know the limits:

- The stride and the channel count come from the **local** config file that heimdall-ctl finds (`--config`, `HEIMDALL_CONFIG`, `./daq_chain_config.ini`, `Firmware/daq_chain_config.ini`). With no config it assumes 5 channels and base ports, and today `--instance` is then ignored.
- `cal-history` and `freq-scan` open the local BerkeleyDB directory read-only. `--host` and `--instance` do not affect them.

**From this release** `--instance N` applies the stride without a config, `cal-history --remote` and `freq-scan --remote` query port 5002, and `fleet ...` subcommands talk to the coordinator.

## Ports, networking and security {#ports-networking-and-security}

### Which ports must I open? {#which-ports-must-i-open}

Open only what your clients need. Per-instance ports are `base + N * port_stride`:

| Port (instance 0) | Service | Bind address | Open it? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1130 | rtl_daq ZMQ tuner control | all interfaces, always | **No.** Local only; unauthenticated, includes a halt command |
| 5000 | iq_server IQ stream | `[daq] listen_address` | only for remote IQ clients, `eth` mode only |
| 5001 | hw_controller control | `listen_address` | only for remote control clients and the coordinator |
| 5002 | status server | `listen_address` | for monitoring, the coordinator and federation peers |
| 5003 | ZMQ event publisher | `listen_address` | for remote event subscribers |
| 6000 | federation coordinator | coordinator setting | only on the coordinator host, for operators |
| 7000 | IQ router output | router setting | only on the router host, for IQ clients |
| 7001 | router stats (this release) | router setting | for monitoring |

No port has authentication today. Bind to a management interface with `[daq] listen_address` and firewall the rest. **From this release** `[daq] zmq_listen_address = 127.0.0.1` restricts port 1130 to loopback, and `auth_token` plus `allow_cidrs` protect ports 6000 and 7001. See `networking_and_time_sync.md`.

### What is the port map for several instances on one host? {#what-is-the-port-map-for-several-instances-on-one-host}

With the default stride of 100:

| Instance | ZMQ | IQ | Control | Status | Events |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 1130 | 5000 | 5001 | 5002 | 5003 |
| 1 | 1230 | 5100 | 5101 | 5102 | 5103 |
| 2 | 1330 | 5200 | 5201 | 5202 | 5203 |
| 3 | 1430 | 5300 | 5301 | 5302 | 5303 |

Keep instance ids between 0 and 9 with stride 100. Instance 10 lands on 6000-6003 and collides with the coordinator. Instance 20 lands on 7000-7003 and collides with the router. The stride must be at least 4 for N > 0 so windows do not overlap. Today `ini_checker` checks only that the stride is positive. **From this release** it warns about these collisions, and treats them as errors for configs that use the new federation keys.

### Are timestamps comparable across hosts? {#are-timestamps-comparable-across-hosts}

Only as well as the hosts' clocks agree. `time_stamp` is the acquiring host's wall clock in milliseconds, taken after USB completion, so it also includes USB and scheduling latency. There is no PPS, GPS or PTP input anywhere in the code. Discipline every host with chrony or PTP if you compare timestamps. Use `cpi_index`, not `time_stamp`, to detect loss within one instance.

## Multiple units and federation {#multiple-units-and-federation}

### Can I run two KrakenSDRs on one Raspberry Pi? {#can-i-run-two-krakensdrs-on-one-raspberry-pi}

Not as a supported setup. Before this release it failed for three independent reasons:

1. rtl_daq opened channel `i` by the hardcoded serial `1000+i`, so two units with factory serials 1000-1004 collided. From this release `[hw] serial_base` / `device_serials` change the mapping (`device_map.c`); the default is still `1000+i`.
2. Every stage reads `daq_chain_config.ini` and several files in `_data_control/` from the current directory, so two instances need two working copies.
3. Each instance pins its four real-time tiers to four cores. A Pi 4 or Pi 5 has four cores, so a second instance stacks SCHED_FIFO tasks on the same cores with RT throttling disabled. A Pi 4 also has a single USB bus for both units, and two units at the shipped rate need about 48 MB/s.

**From this release** the first two problems are solved (`util/set_unit_serials.sh`, `[hw] serial_base`, `util/provision_instance.py`). Also set `[daq] ctr_channel_serial_no` to the unit's first serial (for example 1100 for unit 1). That dongle switches the unit's noise source and bias tees. ini_checker rejects a config where it is not one of the channel serials, and `provision_instance.py` writes it from the template's control-channel index. The core-count rule remains: one hardware instance per 4 cores. The planned preflight check (`daq_preflight.py`, not in the tree yet) is designed to fail a second hardware instance on a 4-core board unless you set `[host] allow_core_sharing = allow`. Use one Pi per unit, or a host with 8 or more cores and separate USB controllers.

### How many instances fit on one host? {#how-many-instances-fit-on-one-host}

Plan with these per-instance figures for a 5-channel unit at 2.4 MS/s and the shipped CPI:

| Resource | Per instance |
|---|---|
