| Dedicated cores | 4 (non-overlapping instances = `floor(nproc / 4)`) |
| USB ingress | 24.0 MB/s |
| Resident `/dev/shm` | about 180 MiB |
| usbfs memory | 30 MiB |
| TCP output in `eth` mode | 96 MB/s (768 Mbit/s) |

An 8-core x86_64 host supports two instances if each unit has its own USB controller. Two `eth` instances exceed one Gigabit link unless you decimate (`R >= 2`) or use shmem output. Also note that `util/irq_tuning.sh` pins every USB interrupt to core 0. See `capacity_planning.md`. **Planned in this release:** `daq_preflight.py` computes these checks for your configs and `heimdall-ctl capacity` wraps it. The `capacity` subcommand exists, but the tool it runs is not in the tree yet.

### How do I run a second instance on one host? {#how-do-i-run-a-second-instance-on-one-host}

Give it its own working copy, its own `instance_id` and its own hardware.

**By hand:**

1. Copy `Firmware/` (with `util/` and `config_files/` beside it) to a second location, for example `/opt/heimdall/instances/1/`.
2. In that copy's `daq_chain_config.ini` set `[federation] instance_id = 1`. Keep `port_stride = 100`.
3. Build the binaries in that copy, or copy them in.
4. Before this release, create `_data_control/inst1_iq_track_lock` containing `0`. From this release `daq_start_sm.sh` creates it.
5. Start it from its own `Firmware/` directory with `sudo ./daq_start_sm.sh`.

Before this release a second KrakenSDR could not be driven because of the serial rule above. From this release reprogram the unit with `util/set_unit_serials.sh` and set `[hw] serial_base` in the copy. The `heimdall-daq@.service` systemd template uses this layout.

**From this release:** `sudo python3 util/provision_instance.py --instance 1 --serial-base 1100 --write` creates a symlinked instance directory, writes the config (including `[host] instance_registry = 1`, `instance_guard = refuse` and a core plan), and prefixes the FIR and hw_caps files. Provision instance 0 with `--in-place` as well on multi-instance hosts. See `deployment_recipes.md`.

### Why does daq_stop.sh stop all instances? {#why-does-daq_stopsh-stop-all-instances}

Because the no-argument form is a host-wide kill by design. `daq_stop.sh` with no argument signals every PID directory of the current working copy and then runs `pkill` by process name (`rtl_daq.out`, `rebuffer.out`, `decimate.out`, `iq_server.out`, `delay_sync.py`, `hw_controller.py`, the synthesizer) across the whole host. External stop scripts rely on this. Source: `daq_stop.sh`.

Stop one instance with its id, from its own working copy:

```bash
sudo ./daq_stop.sh 1
```

Two places called the global form implicitly before this release. `heimdall-daq.service` uses it as `ExecStop`. `daq_start_sm.sh` called it, up to 9 times (the 10th busy check aborts the start), when one of the ports 5000, 5001 or 5002 (+ offset) looked busy. The third port was a hard-coded `5002 + offset`, not the configured `status_server_port`. With `lsof` installed the check used `lsof -i:<port>`, which also matches client sockets, so a DoA client still connected to an old port could make a start kill every instance on the host.

**From this release:** the port check matches only listening sockets (`hd_port_check` in `daq_common.sh`), the supervisor (`daq_supervise.sh`) uses scoped stops, and `daq_stop.sh --this-copy` stops only processes whose working directory is this copy. **Planned in this release:** `heimdall-daq.service` stops instance 0 only (`daq_stop.sh 0`); the shipped unit still calls the global form. The no-argument form stays a global kill.

### Are two KrakenSDRs on different hosts coherent? {#are-two-krakensdrs-on-different-hosts-coherent}

No. Each unit is an independent coherent island. Coherence comes from one shared reference clock, one noise source and one calibration loop inside one rtl_daq and one delay_sync. Two units have independent clocks, so their relative phase is unknown and drifts.

The IQ router does not change this. It interleaves frames from several instances in arrival order and performs no time or sequence alignment today. **From this release** `--align-window-ms` groups frames by `time_stamp`, which requires NTP or PTP on every host. Alignment groups frames in time; it does not make independently clocked units coherent. Process each unit's channels coherently and combine units only at a non-coherent level, for example by fusing bearings. See `theory_coherent_acquisition.md`.

### Does any script start the coordinator or the router? {#does-any-script-start-the-coordinator-or-the-router}

Not today. `daq_start_sm.sh` launches only rtl_daq, rebuffer, decimate, delay_sync, hw_controller and iq_server, and `daq_stop.sh` stops only those. No systemd unit covers the federation services. The coordinator has a command line; the router has none. Start the coordinator by hand:

```bash
cd Firmware
python3 _daq_core/federation_coordinator.py --port 6000 --instances "hosta:0,hostb:0"
```

With `--config`, the coordinator reads `[federation] peer_list`, which by design lists the *other* instances. It therefore omits the instance whose config it reads. Use `--instances` with the full list and without `--config`. When both are given, `--config` wins and `--instances` is ignored. Source: `federation_coordinator.py` (`__main__`).

**From this release:** `./federation_start.sh coordinator|router|all` and `./federation_stop.sh ...` manage both services with PID and log files under `_logs/federation/`, the router gets a full CLI, and systemd units cover them.

### What does REBALANCE do? {#what-does-rebalance-do}

Today, nothing useful. The coordinator's `__main__` never sets a master schedule and no wire verb can set one, so `REBALANCE` distributes nothing and still replies `{"status":"rebalanced","instances":N,"results":{}}`. Even with a schedule set through the Python API, the shipped scheduler without a health monitor assigns everything to instance 0, and schedules of two or more entries travel as a temp-file path that works only on a shared filesystem. Source: `federation_coordinator.py`, `federation_scheduler.py`.

**From this release:**

```text
heimdall-ctl fleet schedule set site.json --strategy round_robin
heimdall-ctl fleet rebalance
heimdall-ctl fleet assignments
```

`SCHEDULE SET` stores the master schedule, `REBALANCE` partitions it across healthy members by node key, large schedules travel in chunks over port 5001 (`SCHB`/`SCHC`/`SCHE`), and each member's load is verified through `SCHG`. Without a master schedule `REBALANCE` replies `{"error":"no master schedule"}`.

### Why does the coordinator report "ok" when an instance is down? {#why-does-the-coordinator-report-ok-when-an-instance-is-down}

Today `federation_health` is computed only over instances that answered. An unreachable instance is excluded from the vote, so a fleet with dead members can still report `ok`. Check the `instances` map for entries carrying `error`. **From this release** unreachable members count as `error`, and `HEALTH` and `fleet status` list them as unreachable.

### Why does the router frame stream stop for every client when one client is slow? {#why-does-the-router-frame-stream-stop-for-every-client-when-one-client-is-slow}

Today the router writes to every output client with a blocking `sendall` while holding one lock. One stalled client blocks forwarding for all clients and, through them, the readers. The router also occupies each instance's single iq_server client slot. **From this release** each client has a bounded queue with a drop policy (`oldest`, `newest`, `disconnect`), slow clients are evicted, and `--connect-on-demand` releases iq_server slots when no client is attached.

### What does "unit_id" mean on a router stream? {#what-does-unit_id-mean-on-a-router-stream}

In the router's default `instance` tag mode, header `unit_id` is overwritten with the source `instance_id`. The physical unit identity from `[hw] unit_id` is lost on the aggregated stream, and instances with the same id on different hosts are indistinguishable. Demultiplex router output by `unit_id` within one host only. **From this release** use `--tag-mode node` and read slot 107 (CRC32 of the source node key), or set `[federation] stamp_node_id = 1` and read slot 108.

### What happens if two coordinators both think they lead? {#what-happens-if-two-coordinators-both-think-they-lead}

This applies only from this release, with `coordinator_candidates` set. With `require_quorum = 0` (default), a network partition can produce two leaders. Each member fences the older term: once a member has seen term `t`, it refuses mutating commands from any coordinator with a lower non-zero term (`stale_term`). With `require_quorum = 1` and at least 3 candidates, the minority side cannot mutate at all (`no_quorum`). If members refuse every command after you wiped a coordinator's state directory, run `daq_stop.sh N --reset-fence` on each member. See `operations_runbook.md`.

## Integration and data {#integration-and-data}

### How do I connect my own DSP application? {#how-do-i-connect-my-own-dsp-application}

Pick one of three interfaces:

| Interface | When to use | How |
|---|---|---|
| Shared memory | DSP on the same host, lowest latency | attach as consumer of `<P>delay_sync_iq` (FIFOs `_data_control/<P>fw_/bw_delay_sync_iq`, segments `_A`/`_B`) |
| TCP port 5000 | DSP on another host | set `out_data_iface_type = eth`, send `streaming`, then `IQDownload` after each frame |
| Router port 7000 | several instances or several clients | read raw `[header][payload]` frames; demultiplex by `unit_id` (or slots 106-108 from this release) |

On every frame, check the sync word, `frame_type` (skip DUMMY, treat CAL separately), `sync_state` and the sync flags. Watch `cpi_index` for gaps. With shmem output, copy the frame before you free the segment, as `capture_shmem_stream.py` does. See `consumer_guide.md`.

### How do I detect lost frames? {#how-do-i-detect-lost-frames}

Use the header counters:

| Signal | Detects |
|---|---|
| a gap in `cpi_index` | drops at the decimator output or later |
| a `daq_block_index` step other than `Ncpi * R / B` between two consecutive DATA frames, with no DUMMY or CAL frame between them and no `cpi_index` gap | a partial CPI discarded upstream |
| an increase of reserved slot 102 | USB ring overruns in rtl_daq (coherence not guaranteed for those frames) |

`daq_block_index` jumps further in normal operation. CAL frames advance it by 1, and the first DATA frame after a DUMMY run or a CAL burst jumps because rebuffer discards its partial CPI there. The two hops before the decimator use backpressure, and an overrun block still gets its index, so use slot 102, not `daq_block_index`, for USB overruns.
| STATUS `counters.dropped_frames_iq` | drops toward your consumer (port 5002) |

Drop warnings are silenced in the C stages by default (`INGORE_FRAME_DROP_WARNINGS 1` in `sh_mem_util.h`), so the logs will not show them. **From this release** `stamp_decimator_drops = 1` puts the decimator drop count in slot 109, and extended STATUS reports the overrun count and continuity gaps.

### Is the FPGA or GPU offload usable? {#is-the-fpga-or-gpu-offload-usable}

No, not end to end. Treat both as experimental. The FIR engine runs only when `decimation_ratio > 1`, so at the shipped `R = 1` neither path executes. The C FPGA engine and the gateware use different SPI framing and register maps. `fpga_loader.py`, which the start scripts call to load a bitstream, defines a class but has no entry point, so the call does nothing. The GPU engine needs `_data_control/fir_shader.bin`, which nothing generates, and falls back to a CPU loop. The Python non-shm transports raise `NotImplementedError`. Use `kfr`, `ne10` or `generic`.

### What does the database keep, and why did my old data vanish? {#what-does-the-database-keep-and-why-did-my-old-data-vanish}

With `[database] en_db = 1`, delay_sync and hw_controller write frame metrics, calibration events, frequency-scan aggregates, hardware snapshots and scheduler position into BerkeleyDB under `db_dir` (default `_db`, relative to the working copy). Rotation prunes records older than `rotation_max_age_hours`. The on-disk format is schema generation 2. A read-write open of a directory with a different or missing generation marker deletes the old files and starts fresh, by design. Records carry no instance id, so give every instance its own `db_dir`.

### How do I upgrade without losing my configuration? {#how-do-i-upgrade-without-losing-my-configuration}

Keep a copy of `daq_chain_config.ini` before you update the tree, because the shipped file is tracked and an update can overwrite it. Then rebuild:

```bash
cp Firmware/daq_chain_config.ini ~/daq_chain_config.ini.bak
# update the tree
cd Firmware/_daq_core && make
cd .. && python3 ini_checker.py daq_chain_config.ini no_hw
```

Run `make` after every update; the start scripts launch `_daq_core/*.out` without checking that they match the sources. PGO profiles survive `make clean` and are not tied to a source revision, so run `make distclean` before a PGO rebuild of new code. `daq_stop.sh --legacy` sends signal 64 (SIGRT) instead of SIGTERM, for binaries built before SIGTERM handling. **From this release** `provision_instance.py --refresh` updates instance directories, and `upgrade_and_rollback.md` covers fleet upgrades and mixed-version clusters.

### Why does ini_checker pass but the chain still fail on my hardware? {#why-does-ini_checker-pass-but-the-chain-still-fail-on-my-hardware}

The start scripts run `ini_checker.py no_hw attached`. `no_hw` skips every hardware probe and the per-channel list-length checks; with no serial keys set it does not check the per-channel serials (`1000+i`). It never checks `ini_version` and never reports unknown keys. **From this release** it validates `peer_list` syntax and `coordinator_host`, the `attached` token adds sysfs checks that every configured serial is attached exactly once and not claimed by another live instance, and in hardware mode (without `no_hw`) with `serial_base` or `device_serials` set it enumerates every device instead of the first five. Without serial keys, hardware mode still checks only that `ctr_channel_serial_no` is one of the serials of the first five devices. Those probes count every Realtek USB device. Run it without `no_hw` on the target host for the hardware checks. Source: `ini_checker.py` (`get_serials`, `_peer_list_findings`, `check_attached_serials`).

### Does the config file name or location ever change? {#does-the-config-file-name-or-location-ever-change}

No. Every stage opens `daq_chain_config.ini` from its current working directory, and there is no command-line or environment override for the pipeline stages. That is why each instance needs its own working copy. heimdall-ctl, a client, also honours `HEIMDALL_CONFIG` and `--config`.
